correctness.rationale: All required hypotheses and normalization are explicit. The exact probability-to-angle identity gives the three-variable inequality. Lagrange multipliers and strict monotonicity of g'' yield the two-equal-coordinate reduction. The boundary and centered cases are controlled analytically, and an exact Sturm variation count (5 at 1/3 and 4 at 1) proves the unique change in the third derivative needed for univariate uniqueness. A deterministic verifier reproduced that count and rational comparisons; 130000 numerical parameter tests and 54000 independent projection hulls corroborated the theorem. Limits are clearly separated from finite tests.

value.rationale: A natural geometric dispersion (de Gua normalized squared right-face areas) is optimally controlled by the probability of a triangular random shadow. The global best constant is strictly below the local Hessian coefficient, with a unique off-center two-equal-leg equality orbit; this distinguishes a meaningful nonlocal angular-rigidity phenomenon from the classical equality-only theorem. The result is self-contained and applicable to shape inference from random views, without claiming statistical robustness.
